project.name: Doshomik
project.footer: Source of truth: the SQL files in `apps/api/migrations/`. Tables, columns and delete rules here were checked against the migrated database on 23 Nov 2026 (migration 005).

labels.softDeleteWhy: The app sets deleted_at. This real DELETE runs when the purge job removes the row after 30 days.
labels.lookup: Delete rules, indexes, migrations and known gaps
labels.hubWhy: Rows connect only because the same person is involved. Usually not what a query means.

areas.name: Accounts & auth
areas.desc: Accounts, signed-in devices, outside sign-in links and one-time email codes.

areas.name: Social & safety
areas.desc: The follow graph, two-way blocks and the moderation queue.

areas.name: Posts & activity
areas.desc: Posts, likes, saves, comments on posts and papers, and the notification inbox.

areas.name: Media
areas.desc: Every upload, whatever uses it. Storage keys only, never URLs.

areas.name: Learn
areas.desc: Topics (concepts), learn items, courses, completions and "I already know this".

areas.name: Practice
areas.desc: Questions by topic, quizzes built from them, and every attempt.

areas.name: Research
areas.desc: Topic chips, the paper collection, bilingual Paper Cards, lineage, saves, the three-step tracker, trails and saved AI outputs.

areas.name: System
areas.desc: The outbox the worker reads and the audit trail. Both outlive what they point at.

users.purpose: One row per account. The hub of the schema.

columns.id: Joins only; never sent to clients
columns.avatar_url: Set by the worker when an avatar upload is ready
columns.follower_count: Stored. Moved ±1 by the worker on `follow.changed`; repaired hourly
columns.totp_enabled_at: Two-factor sign-in; required for staff routes

notes: Profiles read the stored counts instead of running `COUNT(*)` on `follows`.
"People to follow" reads `users_suggest_idx` in order, instead of counting every user's followers and sorting.

sessions.purpose: One row per signed-in device, with a sliding 30-day expiry.

columns.refresh_token_hash: SHA-256 of the secret; replaced on every refresh

notes: Only the token hash is stored, so a leaked row cannot be replayed.

auth_identities.purpose: Links an account to Google or Apple sign-in.

auth_tokens.purpose: One-time codes emailed for verification and password reset.

columns.token_hash: The plain code exists only in the email

notes: Deleted 7 days after expiry or use.

follows.purpose: The follow graph: one row per pair, toggled by status.

columns.status: accepted · pending · **inactive** (new: unfollowed, withdrawn or declined)
columns.updated_at: When the current status began; requests are listed by it

notes: Unfollow, withdraw, decline and block set `inactive` instead of deleting. Following again reactivates the row, and **only the first follow ever notifies**.
Every privacy check already tests `status = 'accepted'`, so `inactive` needs no extra filter there.

blocks.purpose: A block, applied both ways by every visibility check.
notes: Blocking ends follows in both directions (sets them `inactive`).

reports.purpose: The moderation queue: what was reported, by whom, and the outcome.

columns.target_id: **No FK**, on purpose: the report outlives its target
columns.reason: spam · harassment · nudity · violence · misinformation · other

posts.purpose: A text post, an image post or a reel. Visible once its media is ready.

columns.caption: Required for text posts; full-text indexed
columns.topic_id: Concept tag, so a reel can be a Learn before reading link (005)
columns.like_count: Stored. Moved ±1 per like event by the worker (was: full recount)
columns.deleted_at: Hidden at once; purged after 30 days

notes: Feeds are keyset-paginated on `(created_at, id)`, which the two partial indexes cover.

post_likes.purpose: One row per user and post, toggled on and off with is_active.

columns.is_active: false after an unlike; a re-like sets it back

notes: Like = upsert that reactivates the row; unlike = `is_active = false`. An event is written only when the state really changes, and **only the first like ever notifies**.
`is_active` and `updated_at` are in no index, so a toggle is a HOT update with no index writes. Delete + insert wrote two index entries every time.

saved_posts.purpose: A private bookmark list per user.

columns.created_at: Saved list is ordered by this

notes: Deliberately not a toggle row: unsave/re-save has no side effects, and a re-save must move the post to the top, which rewrites the indexed `created_at` anyway.

comments.purpose: A comment on exactly one post or one paper; replies nest through parent_id.

columns.user_id: Nullable: set null on purge so threads survive

notes: The one table shared by the social side and the research side: `paper_id` is a paper's discussion thread (A9), with the same reports, blocks, rate limits and moderation as post comments.
checks: `(post_id IS NULL) <> (paper_id IS NULL)`: exactly one target

notifications.purpose: The inbox: who receives it, who caused it, and what it points at.

columns.type: follow · follow_request · like · comment · reply · post_ready
columns.is_read: Unread rows have their own partial index (new)

notes: Written only by the worker. Re-likes and re-follows no longer add rows here.

media_assets.purpose: Every uploaded image or video: posts, avatars, learn items and paper figures.

columns.playback_key: HLS playlist (video) or WebP base key (image)
columns.duration_ms: Measured by the worker, never taken from the client

notes: Rows at `uploading`/`processing` are the media queue.
The 90-second reel limit is checked in the worker against `duration_ms`.

topics.purpose: A concept, shared by learn items, questions, quizzes, reels, known-topic marks and paper prerequisites.

columns.name: Trigram indexed for fuzzy search
columns.summary: Shown in "Learn first" when a topic has no items yet

learn_items.purpose: One piece of learning content: a video, an image or text.

columns.title: Full-text indexed with `body`
columns.published_at: Set when it first goes live

checks: `kind = 'text' OR media_url IS NOT NULL OR media_id IS NOT NULL`

courses.purpose: An ordered set of learn items, or a link to a free outside course.

columns.external_url: Set for an outside course, which has no items
columns.published_at: Set when it first goes live

course_items.purpose: The ordered steps of a course.
notes: The deferrable key lets a whole course be reordered in one transaction.

course_progress.purpose: How far a user has gone in a course.
notes: Already written with one upsert per save, never delete + insert.

questions.purpose: A multiple-choice or short-answer question in a topic.

columns.published_at: Set when it first goes live

notes: No `created_at` (inherited from Prototype 1).

question_attempts.purpose: Every answer a user submits. Powers history, accuracy and streaks.
notes: Append-only history on purpose: each attempt is its own row.
No `published_at` or `updated_by`, unlike other team content.

quiz_questions.purpose: The ordered questions of a quiz.

fields.purpose: A topic chip (ML fundamentals → … → Emerging research): holds papers, one roadmap, trails and user interests.
notes: A field with papers cannot be deleted (`papers.field_id` restricts).

papers.purpose: The curated collection: staff content plus scholarly metadata ingested by the worker.

columns.title: Full-text indexed with `main_idea`
columns.evaluation: The Prototype 2 summary columns stay; the English card was backfilled from them
columns.openalex_topics: For staff when choosing the chip
columns.search_vector: Title, authors, both card questions; built by `refresh_paper_search()`
columns.published_at: Set when it first goes live

notes: `paper_url` is the main **Open** action (A10): we never host a PDF.
Staff edits win: the worker fills descriptive fields only when empty, and refreshes counts, TLDR and ids every 7 days.

paper_prerequisites.purpose: Learn before reading (A13): the concepts a paper assumes, each with a typed link to our own content.

columns.label: Shown instead of the topic name
columns.why: One line: why it matters here
columns.suggested_by: staff · ai (the app shows a footnote for ai)

notes: **done** is computed: the linked lesson or note is completed, every question of the linked quiz was answered, or the topic is in `user_known_topics`.
checks: `num_nonnulls(learn_item_id, quiz_id, reel_post_id) <= 1`: at most one link

roadmap_steps.purpose: One starting roadmap per field: which papers, in which order, and why.

user_papers.purpose: The Prototype 2 tracker (saved · reading · completed), kept as it was; superseded by paper_saves and reading_passes.
notes: Backfilled into `paper_saves` and `reading_passes` by migration 005. Drop once no client calls `/papers/:id/status`.

user_fields.purpose: The interests a user picked at onboarding.
notes: Saving interests now writes only the difference; before, every save deleted and re-inserted all rows.

paper_cards.purpose: The Paper Card in English and in Bangla (A2, A4 step 1).

columns.question: The paper's question; searched in both languages

notes: Every write calls `refresh_paper_search()` in the same transaction, so search sees it at once.

paper_edges.purpose: Citation lineage inside the collection (A6): what a paper builds on and what built on it.

columns.s2_intents: Semantic Scholar's own labels: background · methodology · result

notes: Semantic Scholar has no supporting or contrasting label. methodology → supporting, background → background, result alone → unknown. **contrasting is set only by staff**, and the worker never overwrites a staff edge.

paper_saves.purpose: The bookmark (A3), independent of reading progress.

columns.created_at: Orders Saved; the earliest unread one is Up next

notes: Up next = saved ∧ no reading pass with step ≥ 1, earliest first.

reading_passes.purpose: The three-step tracker and private note (A4): Explored → Studied → Reproduced.
notes: Lowering the step clears the later times, so "explored this month" never counts a step taken back.
Mark read raises the step to 1 and never lowers it.
checks: `step BETWEEN 0 AND 3`, and each step's time is set exactly while the step holds

research_outputs.purpose: Saved results of the AI research tools (A5, written by Group C), reopened for free.
notes: Opening one reads this row: no AI call, nothing counted against an allowance.

trails.purpose: Reading paths users make (A7): papers in order, one line per step.
notes: Publishing needs at least 2 papers. A published trail follows its author's visibility, like a post, and can be reported.

trail_items.purpose: The ordered steps of a trail.

columns.paper_id: Unique within a trail; published papers only

user_known_topics.purpose: "I already know this": a concept the user marked as known (A13).
notes: This is the spec’s user_known_concepts: our concepts are topics.

learn_item_completions.purpose: Lessons and notes the user completed, wherever they opened them (A13).
notes: Course progress also writes it for the steps reached.

outbox_events.purpose: Work for the worker, written in the same transaction as the change.

columns.entity_id: **No FK**: the event outlives its target
columns.attempts: At 10 the row stays as a dead letter
columns.processed_at: NULL = pending. The worker claims an event by setting it only if still NULL

notes: Each event is claimed and applied in one transaction, so it takes effect exactly once. That is what makes ±1 counter updates safe.

columns.actor_id: Set null when the actor is purged
columns.entity_id: **No FK**: entries outlive what they describe

badges.public_id: Rows have a random `public_id` that the app uses; the internal `id` never leaves the server.
badges.soft delete: Deleting hides a row at once (`deleted_at`); it is removed for good after 30 days.
badges.stored counts: Counts are stored on the row and moved by the worker, instead of counted on every view.
badges.composite PK: The key is a pair of columns, so the same pair can only appear once.
badges.toggle row: One row per pair for ever: it is switched on and off instead of deleted and re-added, so nothing is notified twice.
badges.polymorphic target: It points at different kinds of rows through a plain id, with no foreign key.
badges.no FK: It keeps a plain id with no foreign key, so it outlives what it points at.
badges.tsvector: Its text is indexed for full-text search.
badges.self-reference: Rows can point to other rows of the same table (replies).
badges.work queue: The worker picks up rows from it as jobs.
badges.publishing: Team content: it starts as a draft and the app shows it only once it is published.
badges.deferrable PK: Its position is part of the key and is checked at the end of a transaction, so a whole list can be reordered at once.
badges.ordered: Rows are kept in an order (`position`).
badges.upsert: Each change rewrites the same row instead of adding one.
badges.slug: It has a readable `slug` used in URLs.
badges.pg_trgm: Its name is indexed for typo-tolerant search.
badges.ingested: Some columns are filled by the worker from outside sources, never by the app.
badges.per language: There is one row per language (`en` or `bn`).
badges.typed link: Each row can link to one kind of content: a lesson or note, a quiz, or a reel.
badges.user content: Made by users, so it follows their privacy and can be reported.

indexes.posts_user_id_created_at_idx: A user's posts, any status (also serves the user cascade)
indexes.posts_media_id_idx: Posts waiting on a media asset
indexes.follows_following_id_idx: Who follows me (and the user cascade)
indexes.blocks_blocked_id_idx: Block checks from the blocked side
indexes.post_likes_post_id_idx: Likes per post (repair job, post cascade). is_active is left out on purpose
indexes.comments_paper_id_created_at_idx: Comments per post and paper; reply threads
indexes.comments_parent_id_idx: Comments per post and paper; reply threads
indexes.comments_post_id_created_at_idx: Comments per post and paper; reply threads
indexes.trails_creator_idx: A creator's trails, the public list, trails with a paper
indexes.trails_published_idx: A creator's trails, the public list, trails with a paper
indexes.trail_items_paper_idx: A creator's trails, the public list, trails with a paper

tour.title: The database in one sentence
text: One PostgreSQL database holds everything the app stores: **{tables} tables**, grouped into **{areas} areas**.
This tour shows one idea at a time. You don’t need to remember table names yet.

tour.title: Every row has two ids
text: Each row has an internal number, `id`, that tables use to point at each other.
It also has a random `public_id`. That is the only id the app ever sees, so nobody can guess or count rows from it.

tour.title: Accounts are at the centre
text: `users` has one row per account. {in:users} links from {inFrom:users} tables point to it, more than any other table.
Next to it are the rows that sign a person in: one per device, plus Google sign-in links and one-time email codes.

tour.title: What happens when something is deleted
text: Every link between tables says what happens to a row when the row it points to is deleted. There are only three answers.

visual.cascade: A person’s sessions go with their account. {cascade} links work this way.
visual.setnull: A comment stays as “[deleted]” so replies keep their place. {setnull} links.
visual.restrict: A field with papers in it can’t be deleted. {restrict} links.

tour.title: Following and blocking
text: A follow is one row per pair of people. Unfollowing doesn’t delete it: its status becomes `inactive`, and following again switches it back.
That is why following, unfollowing and following again sends only one notification. A block hides two people from each other everywhere.

tour.title: Posts, likes and comments
text: A post is text, an image or a reel. A like works like a follow: one row per person and post, switched on and off.
Comments live in one table for both posts and papers. Notifications record who did what to whom.

tour.title: Counts are stored, not counted
text: Like, comment and follower counts are numbers kept on the row, so a profile or a post loads without counting anything.
The background worker adds or subtracts one for each change, and checks every hour that the numbers are still right.

tour.title: Uploads
text: Every image and video, whatever it is for, is one row in `media_assets`. The worker processes it and only then can it appear.
The table stores file keys, not web addresses, so the files can move to another storage service without changing data.

tour.title: Learning content
text: A `topic` is one concept, such as “Softmax”. Lessons, notes, quizzes, reels and paper prerequisites all hang off topics.
Courses put learn items in order. The database remembers how far each person got and which lessons they finished.

tour.title: Practice
text: Questions belong to a topic. A quiz is a named set of questions in a fixed order.
Every answer is kept as its own row, which is what accuracy, streaks and “quiz done” are worked out from.

tour.title: The paper collection
text: Papers are grouped by topic chips (`fields`). Each paper has a Paper Card in English and in Bangla.
Citation counts, upvotes and other details come from OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Hugging Face. Only the background worker talks to them; the app just reads our tables.

tour.title: Reading a paper
text: Saving a paper is a bookmark. Reading progress is separate and has three steps, plus a private note only its owner can see.
The first saved paper not yet read is shown as “Up next”.

tour.title: How papers connect
text: Citation links show what a paper builds on and what built on it. Each paper lists the concepts to learn first, each linked to one of our lessons, quizzes or reels.
Anyone can make a trail: a reading path through papers, one line per step.

tour.title: The worker’s to-do list and the record of admin actions
text: When a change needs follow-up work (a notification, a count, an email), the same transaction writes a row to `outbox_events`. The worker works through them in order.
Every admin and security action is written to `audit_log`. Both keep plain ids on purpose, so they outlive what they describe.

tour.title: You’ve seen the whole shape
text: From here, open any area to see its tables, then open a table to see its columns and links one tab at a time.
Reference has the detailed lists: every link, every index, the migrations and the known gaps.

reference.title: Conventions
reference.desc: The patterns almost every table follows

items.title: Internal keys
items.text: `id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`. For joins only; **never sent to clients**.

items.title: Public keys
items.text: `public_id uuid UNIQUE` on every row a client can name.

items.title: Slugs
items.text: `topics.slug` and `fields.slug` name those rows in URLs.

items.title: Enums
items.text: `text` with `CHECK (… IN (…))`. The same lists live in `packages/shared`; change both together.

items.title: Timestamps
items.text: `timestamptz`. `updated_at` is set by the application, not triggers.

items.title: Soft delete
items.text: `deleted_at` on `users`, `posts` and `comments`: hidden at once, purged later.

items.title: Toggle rows
items.text: Relationships that trigger side effects keep one row per pair and flip a state instead of delete + insert: `post_likes.is_active`, `follows.status = 'inactive'`. Only the first activation ever notifies.

items.title: Stored counters
items.text: `posts.like_count`, `comment_count`, `users.follower_count`, `following_count`. Moved ±1 by the worker, exactly once per event; repaired hourly.

items.title: Ingested fields
items.text: Scholarly metadata is written only by the worker. Descriptive fields are filled only when empty, so staff edits win; counts, TLDR and ids refresh every 7 days.

items.title: Languages
items.text: Content that exists per language has `lang` `en` or `bn` (`paper_cards`, `trails`).

items.title: Publishing workflow
items.text: Team content moves `draft → published → archived`. Trails: `draft → published`, and `removed` by a moderator.

items.title: Storage keys, not URLs
items.text: `media_assets` stores keys; URLs are built at read time.

items.title: Ordered children
items.text: `position` in a `DEFERRABLE` primary key (course items, quiz questions, roadmap steps, trail items), so a list can be reordered in one transaction.

items.title: Polymorphic references
items.text: `reports.target_id`, `outbox_events.entity_id`, `audit_log.entity_id`: no FK on purpose.

reference.desc: What is indexed, and for which screen

reference.desc: Checks on values, and the errors the API returns

items.title: Post media
items.text: `type = 'text' OR media_id IS NOT NULL`

items.title: Comment target
items.text: `(post_id IS NULL) <> (paper_id IS NULL)`

items.title: MCQ options
items.text: `kind = 'short' OR cardinality(options) >= 2`

items.title: Learn item media
items.text: `kind = 'text' OR media_url IS NOT NULL OR media_id IS NOT NULL`

items.title: Follow status
items.text: `status IN ('accepted', 'pending', 'inactive')`; no self-follow

items.title: No self-block
items.text: `blocker_id <> blocked_id`

items.title: Reading steps
items.text: `step BETWEEN 0 AND 3`; each step's time set exactly while the step holds; note ≤ 400 characters

items.title: One link at most
items.text: `num_nonnulls(learn_item_id, quiz_id, reel_post_id) <= 1`

items.title: No self-citation
items.text: `citing_paper_id <> cited_paper_id`

items.title: Counts
items.text: `citation_count >= 0`, `hf_upvotes >= 0`, `trend_rank > 0`

head: When the database refuses
The API answers
rows: CHECK, NOT NULL or bad format

reference.title: How data changes and expires
reference.desc: Status flows, and what is cleaned up when

items.title: Like
items.text: One row for ever. Only the first activation notifies; each real change moves `like_count` by one.

items.title: Follow
items.text: `pending` for private accounts until accepted. Unfollow, withdraw, decline and block all go to `inactive`.

items.title: Reading pass
items.text: Cumulative. Lowering a step clears the later step times. Mark read only raises to 1.

items.title: Trail
items.text: Publishing needs 2+ papers. `removed` is a moderator action.

items.title: Paper ingestion
items.text: Import or "sync now" queue a paper; the worker's papers loop takes 10 a minute.

items.title: Media asset
items.text: The worker measures duration and builds variants.

items.title: Post
items.text: `removed` is a moderator action, separate from `deleted_at`.

items.title: Team content
items.text: Papers, courses, learn items, questions and quizzes.

sections.title: What is cleaned up, and when

items.title: Deleted accounts
items.text: Hidden at once. After 30 days: comments become `[deleted]`, the user row is deleted (cascading), their media is removed, and a `user.purge` audit entry is written.

items.title: Deleted posts
items.text: Hidden at once; row and media deleted after 30 days.

items.title: Stored counters
items.text: Post and follow counts recounted wherever they drifted (mainly after purges).

items.title: Inactive likes and follows
items.text: Kept: they are what stops re-notification. They go when the user or post is purged.

items.title: Research order
items.text: `trend_rank` recomputed hourly and after every ingestion round.

items.title: Paper metadata
items.text: Refreshed from the sources every 7 days per paper; a failed sync keeps `sync_error` and is retried after 7 days or on "sync now".

items.title: Reading passes, saves, outputs, trails
items.text: Kept until the user or the paper is deleted.

items.title: Abandoned uploads
items.text: `uploading`/`failed` assets older than 1 day that nothing uses.

items.title: Sessions
items.text: Expired or revoked more than 30 days ago.

items.title: Email codes
items.text: Expired or used more than 7 days ago.

items.title: Outbox events
items.text: Processed more than 30 days ago. Events with 10 failed attempts stay as dead letters.

items.title: Raw uploads
items.text: Deleted as soon as processing ends (they hold GPS and camera metadata).

reference.title: Research tab features
reference.desc: Each feature of the spec and the tables behind it (migration 005)

sections.intro: Group A of the Research spec, feature by feature. Open one to see what existed and what was added.

items.title: A1: Paper collection, topic chips, trending order
text: **Already there:** Papers in a field (fields = chips); newest-first list
**Added:** Scholarly metadata on `papers`, `fields.position`, ingestion worker (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Hugging Face), `trend_rank`, default `?sort=trend`

items.title: A2: Search papers (EN + BN)
text: **Already there:** English full text on title + main idea
**Added:** `paper_cards` per language, `papers.search_vector` over title, authors and both card questions, `bangla` configuration

items.title: A3: Save / bookmark, "Up next"
text: **Already there:** "saved" was a tracker status
**Added:** `paper_saves`; `GET /me/papers/up-next`

items.title: A4: Three-step tracker and private note
text: **Already there:** saved · reading · completed
**Added:** `reading_passes`: step 0–3, per-step times, 400-character note, monthly counts

items.title: A5: My papers
text: **Already there:** —
**Added:** Saved / Read lists; `research_outputs` reopened without AI

items.title: A6: Related papers: lineage
text: **Already there:** "Related" by shared topics
**Added:** `paper_edges` with intent; `GET /papers/:id/lineage`; staff-only `contrasting`

items.title: A7: Creator reading paths (trails)
text: **Already there:** Staff roadmap, one per field
**Added:** `trails`, `trail_items`; reportable and moderated

items.title: A9: Discussion, comments, moderation
text: **Already there:** **Complete**: `comments.paper_id`, reports, blocks, rate limits, cursors, moderation
**Added:** Nothing (upvotes wait for A15)

items.title: A10: Open the original paper
text: **Already there:** `paper_url`
**Added:** `pdf_url`, `arxiv_id`, `links.open_url`

items.title: A13: Prerequisite → Learn matching
text: **Already there:** Prerequisite topics with their learn items
**Added:** Label, why, typed link and `suggested_by` on `paper_prerequisites`; `user_known_topics`; `learn_item_completions`; `posts.topic_id`; computed `done`

items.title: Ingestion (worker only)
items.text: Then `trend_rank`. Hugging Face daily papers every 6 h set upvotes, trending and code links.

items.title: Search
items.text: Query: `websearch_to_tsquery('english', q) || websearch_to_tsquery('bangla', q)`.

items.title: Reading loop
items.text: Counts per month feed Profile → Reading.

items.title: Learn before reading
items.text: Done = completed lesson or note, every quiz question answered, or "I already know this".

items.title: Semantic Scholar intents
items.text: Its labels are background, methodology and result: no supporting or contrasting. Mapped without guessing; `contrasting` comes only from staff (`PUT /admin/paper-edges`).

items.title: Edges only inside the collection
items.text: Every lineage row must be tappable. Built from each paper's own references, so every pair in the collection is found.

items.title: Trend rank
items.text: HF trending in the last 14 days first (most upvotes), then most cited, then newest. Stored as a dense 1..n for a cheap keyset page.

items.title: Staff edits win
items.text: Ingestion fills title, authors, venue, abstract only when empty; an import's empty title is filled on its first sync.

items.title: Existing tables kept
items.text: `user_papers` and the Prototype 2 summary columns on `papers` are unchanged; the new tables were backfilled from them.

items.title: bangla = simple
items.text: PostgreSQL ships no Bangla stemmer. Word splitting depends on the server locale; a C locale keeps every Bangla sign in the word.

items.title: Concept = topic
items.text: `user_known_concepts` of the spec is `user_known_topics`; reels get `posts.topic_id`.

items.title: Likes are toggle rows
items.before: Unlike deleted the row; a re-like inserted a new one and sent the author a new notification and push every time. Like → unlike → like could spam.
items.after: One row per user and post with `is_active`. Unlike sets it false, re-like sets it true. Only the first like ever notifies. The toggle is a HOT update (no index writes).

items.title: Follows are toggle rows
items.before: Unfollow, withdraw, decline and block deleted the row, so following again re-sent the follow / request notification.
items.after: Status `inactive` keeps the row; following again reactivates it. Only the first follow ever notifies. Requests are listed by `updated_at`, the time they were (re)sent.
items.where: users.service.ts follow / unfollow / accept / decline / block

items.title: Counters move by one instead of recounting
items.before: Every like, unlike, comment or comment delete made the worker `COUNT(*)` all likes *and* all comments of the post: O(n) per event on a busy post.
items.after: The worker adds or subtracts 1. It claims each event (`processed_at IS NULL`) in the same transaction, so a delta is applied exactly once. The hourly repair still catches drift.
items.where: worker/outbox.ts · moderation only emits comment.deleted for a live comment

items.title: Stored follower and following counts
items.before: Every profile view ran two `COUNT(*)` over `follows`. "People to follow" counted followers for *every* active user, then sorted them.
items.after: `users.follower_count` / `following_count`, moved by `follow.changed` events. Suggestions read `users_suggest_idx` in order and stop after the limit.
items.where: migration 004 · users.service.ts getProfile / suggestUsers · worker follow.changed

items.title: Interests write only the difference
items.before: Saving interests deleted every row and inserted them all again, even when nothing changed.
items.after: Removed fields are deleted, new ones inserted; unchanged rows are left alone.

items.title: Index for the unread badge
items.before: The unread count scanned all of a user's notifications through `(user_id, created_at)`.
items.after: `notifications_unread_idx (user_id) WHERE NOT is_read`: only unread rows.

items.title: Redundant reels index dropped
items.before: The Prototype 1 index `posts (created_at DESC) WHERE type = 'reel'` sat beside `posts_reels_idx`, which covers the same order with the filters the query uses.
items.after: Dropped: one less index to write on every reel insert.

sections.title: Looked at and left as they are

items.title: saved_posts
items.text: Not toggled: unsaving has no side effects, and a re-save must move the post to the top of the list, which rewrites the indexed `created_at` anyway.

items.title: user_papers, course_progress
items.text: Already one upsert on the same row.

items.title: blocks
items.text: Rare, with no side effects. Delete + insert is fine.

items.title: question_attempts
items.text: Append-only by design: each attempt is history.

items.title: posts_count on profiles
items.text: Still `COUNT(*)`, served by the partial feed index. Store it if profiles get hot.

reference.title: Migrations
reference.desc: The six SQL files, in order

items.title: 1. 1795305600000_prototype-v1-schema.sql
items.text: The Prototype 1 schema: 16 tables, `pg_trgm`, search indexes.

items.title: 2. 1795305600001_prototype-2.sql
items.text: The Prototype 2 appendix SQL (14 new tables): public ids, slugs, user status and privacy, media, publishing, auth, safety, outbox, audit.

items.title: 3. 1795305600002_prototype-2-backfill.sql
items.text: Slugs `NOT NULL`; post media into `media_assets`; drops `posts.media_url`; relaxes the learn item media check.

items.title: 4. 1795305600003_sessions-public-id-and-2fa.sql
items.text: `sessions.public_id`, two-factor columns, and indexes for feed, reels, saves and follow requests.

items.title: 5. 1795305600004_toggles-and-stored-counts.sql
items.text: Toggle rows for likes and follows, stored follow counts, the unread and suggestion indexes, and drops the redundant reels index. See [Efficiency (004)](#changes).

items.title: 6. 1795305600005_research-collection.sql
items.text: Research tab Group A: the `bangla` search configuration, paper metadata and `search_vector`, `paper_cards`, `paper_saves`, `reading_passes`, `research_outputs`, `paper_edges`, `trails`, `trail_items`, Learn before reading links, `user_known_topics`, `learn_item_completions`. 9 new tables. See [Research (005)](#research).

sections.note: Never edit a migration that has been applied: add a new one. After a schema change, regenerate `src/db/types.ts` with `pnpm db:types`.

items.title: Random UUIDv4 public ids
items.text: Switch to `uuidv7()` on PostgreSQL 18 for better index locality.

items.title: One worker only (advisory lock)
items.text: Lease columns plus `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. The claim step already makes a second worker harmless.

items.title: Counter repair scans every row hourly
items.text: Run it daily, or only for posts and users touched by purges.
items.tag: at hundreds of thousands of posts

items.title: Practice stats aggregate all attempts
items.text: A per-user, per-topic stats table updated by the worker.
items.tag: when users have thousands of attempts

items.title: Random practice questions use `ORDER BY random()`
items.text: Sample by id range or `TABLESAMPLE`.
items.tag: at tens of thousands of questions

items.title: `user_papers` duplicates the new tracker
items.text: Drop it and `/papers/:id/status` once no client uses them.

items.title: Bangla search is unstemmed
items.text: Give the `bangla` configuration a real dictionary; queries stay the same.

items.title: Contrasting citations only by hand
items.text: A source with citation stances, if one becomes affordable.

items.title: No discovery queue for new papers
items.text: A `paper_candidates` table from Hugging Face daily papers, reviewed by staff.

items.title: Comment upvotes on paper discussion
items.text: `comment_votes` plus a stored count, with Paper Clubs (A15).

items.title: Research Groups B and C
items.text: They write `paper_cards` (source ai), `paper_prerequisites` (suggested_by ai) and `research_outputs`.

items.title: Search runs on Postgres
items.text: Elasticsearch indexer reading the existing `search.sync` events.

items.title: No user locale
items.text: `users.locale` for Bangla push and email.

items.title: One DB role with full rights
items.text: DML-only app role, DDL migration role, PgBouncer, PITR backups.

items.title: Large tables
items.text: Partition `notifications` and `question_attempts`; read replica.
